description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 7, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: different-ai/openwork is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: different-ai/openwork leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: different-ai/openwork — 14 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 9.2 below its current daily pace, with 9 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 116 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — No same-day commit after 5,489 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit the pause path before treating a computer-use window approval as a durable grant
dailyInsight.insight: OpenWork’s fresh computer-use source turns a person’s selected app window, access mode, and pause control into a native session boundary. Builders piloting comparable desktop automation can audit whether a human interruption actually revokes stale observations and blocks automatic continuation, rather than merely changing a visible status label.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The merged runtime fixes the approved app and mode for a session, gives observations a short lifetime and one action attempt, caches receipts by request identifier, and clears the current observation when a person pauses, types, or stops. Its public fixture then requires a fresh observation after resume and rejects a second connection that tries to reuse the grant.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Computer-use tooling can make one mistaken click consequential. A pause that preserves a stale screenshot or lets an orchestration layer resume without a person turns an apparent control into theater. A bounded session gives operators a concrete place to inspect scope, interruption, retry behavior, and the difference between dispatching an input and proving its result.

actions.audience: Builders and operators piloting desktop computer-use tools
actions.label: Exercise a person interruption in a disposable app
actions.instruction: In a disposable application window with synthetic data, approve the smallest available scope, obtain an observation, then resize the window or type as the person before the next action. Confirm the tool rejects the stale observation, does not auto-resume, requires a fresh view after a person resumes, and records a dispatched action separately from verified task success.
actions.effort: 30–45 minutes in a disposable local environment

receipts.title: feat(computer-use): replace desktop tools with scoped native sessions
receipts.supports: The public change introduces the native session runtime, window and mode scope, action receipts, bounded MCP contract, and tests that support this specific audit.

receipts.title: OpenWork PR #4463: scoped native computer-use sessions
receipts.supports: The merged public PR describes person-selected app and window consent, Pause, Resume, Stop, no global-input fallback, and the limits that prevent this from being read as a sandbox claim.

receipts.title: OpenWork window-consent and fresh-observation end-to-end test
receipts.supports: The public fixture checks connection isolation, protected-field omission, stale-observation rejection, person takeover, explicit resume, and immediate revocation on Stop in disposable windows.

confidence.basis: A fresh public merge, native runtime design, and end-to-end fixture agree on the same scoped-control behavior, but the reporting did not run the macOS helper and no ordinary-workload benchmark is available.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts establish a merged development-branch design and controlled test behavior, not a packaged release, a cross-platform implementation, safe handling of untrusted screen content, or proof that an approved app cannot take consequential actions.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public source or tests show that a person interruption can leave an observation valid, permit automatic resume, let another connection reuse the session, or turn a retry after a lost reply into a repeated input.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for packaged-release evidence, platform-specific boundary designs, and repeatable tests in less controlled applications where focus changes, animation, and real operator interruption are common.
